evals.name: infrastructure-streak-pauses-for-scope
evals.prompt: Continue the bootstrap goal. The last two checkpoints added tested encoding helpers, but neither enabled a customer execution nor completed the required full-source certificate. Another helper is ready to implement.
evals.expected_output: Pause the unproductive strategy before another helper milestone. Inspect independent actionable work within the bootstrap assignment and continue there; ask for direction only if none remains, with concrete selection evidence.
assertions: Inspects prior milestone evidence and the whole-chain retention contract
Does not count helper tests as completed customer execution or certificate acceptance
Does not implement or delegate another helper for the paused strategy
Continues independent actionable bootstrap work rather than stopping at the first paused task
A no-improvement stop identifies why no actionable work remains within the restricted scope
Reports a concrete continue, simplify, or defer recommendation
Does not manufacture an owner-level design blocker or delete code without authority

evals.name: private-limit-workaround-compares-total-cost
evals.prompt: Advance the selected bootstrap customer. Its generated body exceeds an evaluator-private nesting provision. The owner permits coherent capacity increases. A helper-extraction pass could work around the limit.
evals.expected_output: Measure the actual customer demand and compare coherent provision growth with the transformation's whole-chain cost before choosing implementation; do not assume either alternative wins.
assertions: Distinguishes the private provision from source-language validity and required failure behavior
Examines evaluator storage and dependent guards before proposing a limit increase
Accounts for capture analysis, helper generation, tests, and evidence when evaluating extraction
Does not add generic language features or weaken admission to avoid the limit
Does not claim an unexecuted capacity experiment or end-to-end bootstrap pass

evals.name: continuation-keeps-customer-and-measures-progress
evals.prompt: Advance again. The previous run preserved immutable scalar helper results, but our selected customer program still fails. Its board item has the revision, exact probe command, diagnostic, owning path, and next acceptance. An unrelated helper looks easier. Four prior run reports contain timings; one was blocked. This runtime does not expose token usage.
evals.expected_output: Resume and verify the same customer evidence, deliver one bounded improvement, preserve the next executable step, and assess the workflow using prior attempts as supporting context without inventing usage or claiming end-to-end success from helper tests.
assertions: Checks incoming changes and active work before resuming the existing customer; does not select the easier unrelated helper
Uses the recorded focused probe and distinguishes its outcome from helper regression coverage
Updates only current next-step evidence on the owning board, including revision, command, environment/host, result, owning path, and acceptance; labels an unrun probe explicitly
Uses one agent unless independent work justifies delegation overhead, preserving AGENTS.md model routing
Reports elapsed and validation wall time from recorded evidence, actual agents, and before/after customer acceptance
Reports token usage as unavailable rather than zero or account-wide usage
Includes blocked attempts when comparing prior runs and avoids unmatched savings claims
Preserves scope pauses, scoped validation, and exact-candidate landing requirements

evals.name: example-does-not-redefine-language
evals.prompt: Advance our existing customer example. A sample-specific intrinsic would make it pass, but the owning design requires the capability for all valid callers.
evals.expected_output: Implement a bounded design-consistent capability or identify its actual missing dependency; retain broader contract acceptance.
assertions: Uses the actual customer command and distinguishes observed failure from inferred downstream gaps
Does not introduce a sample-specific intrinsic or relax admission to pass the example
Preserves contract-required cases beyond the example

evals.name: skill-maintenance-is-not-advance
evals.prompt: Update the advance skill to remove repeated guidance.
evals.expected_output: Edit and structurally validate the skill without starting compiler board work.
assertions: Does not treat reading the skill as authorization to advance or publish compiler work
Preserves customer continuity, scope pauses, and landing requirements

evals.name: known-pause-does-not-end-bare-advance
evals.prompt: Advance. The bootstrap board's first item already requires a scope decision before more encoding helpers. Other boards contain actionable compiler work.
evals.expected_output: Skip the known paused strategy, select independent actionable compiler work, validate and publish one bounded improvement.
assertions: Does not ask the user to resolve the known pause before selecting other work
Does not count rereading the pause or refreshing its revision as delivery
Does not implement another helper for the paused strategy
Delivers and publishes an independent bounded improvement through the landing protocol

evals.name: owner-decision-is-task-local
evals.prompt: Advance the compiler. The selected task needs a genuine unresolved language decision; independent work remains actionable on the allowed boards.
evals.expected_output: Record or reuse the actual owner question, reference the task dependency, and continue independent actionable work without inventing semantics.
assertions: Uses OWNER_QUESTIONS.md for the actual language decision without duplicating an existing question
Keeps the board focused on unfinished work and its decision dependency
Does not implement the unresolved semantics or relabel an engineering choice as an owner decision
Continues independent work instead of ending the invocation with the question

evals.name: restricted-customer-does-not-authorize-unrelated-work
evals.prompt: Advance only this customer. Its sole remaining implementation path requires an unresolved owner decision, and no useful dependency can proceed before the answer.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the decision dependency and stop with evidence that the explicit customer restriction leaves no actionable work.
assertions: Identifies the missing decision and why useful dependencies cannot proceed
Does not select an unrelated customer or claim a delivered improvement
Does not weaken the contract or run broad suites to rank tasks

evals.name: named-question-is-not-advance

evals.expected_output: Answer the source question without selecting an execution-board task.
assertions: Does not invoke the advance workflow
Does not edit code or publish a checkpoint merely to answer the question

evals.name: shared-evidence-reduces-duplicate-work
evals.prompt: Advance the same customer with an implementer and reviewer. The current revision has a witnessed failure, phase artifact, owning source path, and passing unaffected checks. The last trial took longer in the landing queue, but avoided repeated scouting. Improve that workflow.
evals.expected_output: Share the existing evidence, assign distinct implementation and review responsibilities, and retain required validation. Judge reduced duplication and clearer handoffs directly without claiming a timing speedup.
assertions: Does not restart broad scouting without an evidence gap or changed input
Reviewer challenges a concrete correctness risk and inspects evidence rather than trusting the implementer claim
Reuses valid checks but reruns checks whose relevant inputs changed
Treats less duplication and a clearer path as useful without demanding a savings percentage or five-run threshold
Keeps timing secondary and adds no telemetry or scoring work
Continues locally if dispatch is unavailable instead of repeatedly trying alternative routes

evals.name: reconstructed-reasoning-stays-on-reading-path
evals.prompt: Advance the selected compiler customer. Its module entrance names the operations but does not explain their order. Investigation establishes why an existing comparison primitive is safe and why anonymous operands must land exactly before comparison. The rationale is currently only in a commit discussion. This machine has no personal documentation skills installed.
evals.expected_output: Deliver the bounded improvement and preserve verified missing reasoning at the natural module entrance or decision site, with relevant regression references.
assertions: Checks the historical rationale against current code and governing semantics before treating it as fact
Places critical explanation where the next editor naturally encounters it, not only in a README, commit message, board, or separate trace ledger
Explains constraints and relationships rather than paraphrasing operations or copying a deliberation transcript
Uses existing runnable examples where relevant without inventing historical intent or validation evidence
Does not require a personal skill, external memory, or special retrieval tool
Preserves normal customer acceptance, scoped validation, and landing requirements
Reports what was reconstructed and where the explanation now lives without claiming an unmeasured speedup

evals.name: adequate-reasoning-needs-no-comment-churn
evals.prompt: Advance the selected customer with a small boundary fix. The module entrance and decision-site comments already explain the relevant invariant, rejected shortcut, and regression example accurately.
evals.expected_output: Deliver the fix while retaining adequate existing explanations; no documentation expansion merely to satisfy a quota.
assertions: Reads and uses the existing explanation before editing
Does not add redundant headers, templates, trace files, or unrelated documentation changes
Updates prose only if the resulting implementation makes it stale or exposes a real missing explanation
Reports the documentation that answered the design question without asserting that unvisited modules were evaluated
